title: Mean Squared Error
statement: Implement `mse(y_true, y_pred)`, the mean squared error between two equal-length sequences. Average the squared residuals. Do not take a square root; that is RMSE.

approaches.name: Direct average
approaches.explanation: MSE is the empirical risk for squared loss. The factor 1/n makes the number comparable across batch sizes.

editorial: MSE = (1/n) Σ (yᵢ − ŷᵢ)². Squaring penalizes large misses more than absolute error and gives a smooth gradient 2(ŷ − y)/n with respect to the prediction. Divide by n so a longer test set does not inflate the metric. RMSE is the square root of this value and lives in the original units of y.
reference_solution:
def mse(y_true: list[float], y_pred: list[float]) -> float:
    return float(sum((a - b) ** 2 for a, b in zip(y_true, y_pred)) / len(y_true))
